props.gloss_en: Rava: 'from the people' -- not from the priests; when it says 'from those who slaughter the slaughter' -- even a priest-butcher is included
the source: 'from those who slaughter the slaughter' (Deut 18:3) includes a priest-butcher
R' Tavla to his priest host: go partner with the Israelite butchers -- since they are exempted from the gifts, they will partner with you
Rav Nachman obligated him [in the gifts]: go give them out
the elders of the south: a priest-butcher is exempt from the gifts two or three weeks; from then on he is obligated
Rav Nachman: that [exemption] is where he did not establish a butcher shop; but here he did establish one
Rav Chisda: a priest who does not separate the gifts -- let him be under the ban of the God of Israel
Rabba bar Rav Shila: these butchers of Huzal have stood under Rav Chisda's ban these twenty-two years
reading 1 of Rabba bar Rav Shila's statement: that we no longer ban them

the baraita: when is this said? of a prohibition; but of a positive mitzva -- e.g. they tell him 'make a sukka' and he does not, 'lulav' and he does not, 'make tzitzit' and he does not -- they strike him until his soul departs
reading 2: rather, that we fine them without a warning
Rava fined a thigh
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak fined a cloak
Rav Chisda: the foreleg to one [priest], the maw to one, the jaw to two
Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef: in the West we divide them bone by bone
R' Yochanan: it is forbidden to eat from an animal whose gifts were not lifted
R' Yochanan: whoever eats from an animal whose gifts were not lifted is as though he eats untithed produce
the halakha is not as R' Yochanan [on eating from an animal whose gifts were not lifted]
Rav Chisda: the priestly gifts are eaten only roasted, and only with mustard
what is the reason? the verse says 'for anointing' (Num 18:8) -- for greatness, as kings eat
Rav Chisda: [there are] twenty-four priestly gifts; any priest who is not expert in them -- one does not give him a gift

R' Shimon: any priest who does not acknowledge the service has no share in the priesthood, as it says 'he among the sons of Aaron who offers the blood of the peace offering and the fat -- his shall be the right thigh for a portion' (Lev 7:33)
R' Shimon's verse: 'he who offers the blood ... shall have the right thigh' (Lev 7:33)

the baraita continues: I have only this [rite]; from where to include fifteen services -- the pourings, mixings, crumblings, saltings, wavings, bringings, handfuls, burnings, pinchings, receivings, sprinklings, giving the sota to drink, breaking the heifer's neck, the leper's purification and lifting the hands, inside or outside? the verse says 'of the sons of Aaron' -- any service stated of the sons of Aaron; and any priest who does not acknowledge it has no share in the priesthood
the reason is that he does not acknowledge it; but if he acknowledges it -- [he has a share] even though he is not expert in them
Rav: the veins in the jaw are forbidden
Rav: and any priest who does not know how to remove them -- one does not give him a gift
a priest who seizes the gifts -- is he showing fondness for the mitzva or contempt for it? Rava resolved: 'and he shall give' (Deut 18:3) -- not that he take by himself
Abaye: at first I would seize the gifts; I said: I am showing fondness for the mitzva
Abaye (stage 2): I did not seize; I would say 'give me'
Abaye: once I heard 'and he shall give' -- not that he take by himself -- I no longer seized
the baraita: 'and they turned aside after gain' (I Sam 8:3) -- R' Meir says: the sons of Samuel asked for their portion with their mouths
Abaye (stage 3): I did not say [give me] either; but if they gave me, I took
Abaye: once I heard R' Meir's baraita on the sons of Samuel, I no longer said 'give me'
the baraita: the modest withdraw their hands, and the gluttons divide
Abaye (stage 4): I did not take either, except on the eve of Yom Kippur
Abaye: once I heard the baraita 'the modest withdraw their hands', I did not take either
Abaye: [I took on the eve of Yom Kippur] to establish myself among the priests

Rav Yosef: a priest who has a young Torah scholar in his neighbourhood who is hard-pressed -- let him grant him the gifts, even though they have not come into his hand, with the acquaintances of the priesthood and Levites
Rava told the attendant: grant us the gifts, for I want to eat tongue with mustard; he granted it to him; Rava ate
and Rav Safra did not eat
they read to Rav Safra in a dream: 'as one who removes a garment on a cold day, vinegar on natron, so is one who sings songs to a sad heart' (Prov 25:20)
Rav Safra: perhaps it was read to me because I transgressed the Master's ruling?
Rav Yosef: when I said it, [it was] of another; the attendant grants against his will
Rav Yosef: and when I said it, [it was] of one who cannot [otherwise]; this one can
then why was it read to me? -- [it was directed] toward Rava
Abaye to Rav Dimi: of what is the verse's plain sense written? RD: of one who teaches an unworthy student

Rav: whoever teaches an unworthy student falls into Gehenna, as it says 'all darkness is laid up for his treasures; a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that remains (sarid) in his tent' (Job 20:26)
Rav: and 'sarid' is none but a Torah scholar, as it says 'and among the remnant (sridim) whom the Lord calls' (Joel 3:5)

Rav (via R' Zeira): whoever teaches an unworthy student is like one who throws a stone to Markulis, as it says 'as a stone bound in a sling (margema), so is he who gives honour to a fool' (Prov 26:8), and it is written 'luxury is not seemly for a fool' (Prov 19:10)
